Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    # Find the solid zero canvases, extending their rectangle to include embedded pattern marks.
    # A canvas is an axis-aligned rectangle bounded by color 8, with zeros plus one seed color.
    for color in range(1,10):
        pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]==color]
        if not pts: continue
        # derive canvas bounds from nearest enclosing 8 border: flood component through 0 and color
        allowed={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c] in (0,color)}
        seen=set(); comps=[]
        for p in pts:
            if p in seen: continue
            q=[p]; seen.add(p); comp=[]
            while q:
                r,c=q.pop(); comp.append((r,c))
                for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    z=(r+dr,c+dc)
                    if z in allowed and z not in seen: seen.add(z); q.append(z)
            comps.append(comp)
        # Seeds are separated by 8 only if no zero connection; choose region with largest bbox containing seed.
        # Regions may be joined to unrelated zeros; split using the local rectangular 0 area bounded by 8.
        for r,c in pts:
            # expand rectangle from seed while adjacent rows/columns are 0 or this color
            # take maximal contiguous rectangle of allowed cells containing seed
            top=bottom=r; left=right=c
            changed=True
            while changed:
                changed=False
                if top>0 and all(g[top-1][x] in (0,color) for x in range(left,right+1)): top-=1; changed=True
                if bottom+1<H and all(g[bottom+1][x] in (0,color) for x in range(left,right+1)): bottom+=1; changed=True
                if left>0 and all(g[y][left-1] in (0,color) for y in range(top,bottom+1)): left-=1; changed=True
                if right+1<W and all(g[y][right+1] in (0,color) for y in range(top,bottom+1)): right+=1; changed=True
            # only act if this encloses the seed and is a genuine canvas > seed footprint
            if (bottom-top+1)*(right-left+1)<12: continue
            # collect pattern coordinates (seed color) within rectangle, using bounding box of seed shape
            local=[(y,x) for y,x in pts if top<=y<=bottom and left<=x<=right]
            if not local: continue
            pr0=min(y for y,x in local); pr1=max(y for y,x in local)
            pc0=min(x for y,x in local); pc1=max(x for y,x in local)
            ph,pw=pr1-pr0+1,pc1-pc0+1
            mask={(y-pr0,x-pc0) for y,x in local}
            for y in range(top,bottom+1):
                for x in range(left,right+1):
                    g[y][x]=color if ((y-pr0)%ph,(x-pc0)%pw) in mask else 0
            break
    return g
